text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malaysian ambassador to Peru, Ahmad Mokhtar Selat who was released on Saturday by Peruvian Marxist rebels holding the Japanese ambassador's residence under siege, said he would take a short break before returning to his duties in Lima. Ahmad said he was in "good health".
- Road links to storm-ravaged Keningau in the eastern Malaysian state of Sabah from state capital Kota Kinabalu have been restored.

- Chief minister of Selangor state, Muhammad Muhammad Taib, said he will call a meeting of the state's United Malay National Organisation's (Malaysia's dominant political party) liason committee to explain his arrest by Australian authorities last week. Muhammad Taib was arrested at Brisbane airport for allegedly failing to declare the equivalent of 2.4 million ringgit in cash he was carrying with him.

- Malaysian property company Berjaya Industrial Bhd has bought a 17 percent stake in Promet Bhd and 32 percent stake in Kelanamas Industries Bhd for 350 million ringgit and 314.5 million ringgit respectively.

- Kuala Lumpur motorists will face higher toll charges for using the North-South Expressway from Wednesday, making it the second toll rate hike in four months. The rise is part of a three-phase staggered toll increase implemented in September by concession-holder Projek Lebhraya Utara Selatan (PLUS). The rate will go up to 10.5 cents per kilometre, an increase of 1.5 cents.
